Let's follow the standard five-step procedure.

**Step 1:** We are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=-5\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2:** Form the matrix of the minors of $A.$
To make this matrix, we replace each entry of $A$ by its minor.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-17 & -12 & -3 \\ -4 & -4 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3:** Create the matrix of cofactors by changing the sign of some of the entries of $M$ according to the rule of alternating signs.

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-17 & 12 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 4:** Write down the transpose of the matrix of cofactors.

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-17 & 4 & -1 \\ 12 & -4 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 5:** Use the formula for the inverse of a $3\times 3$ matrix.

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-17 & 4 & -1 \\ 12 & -4 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
